newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas sees first Mar '98 deals, nearbys slip.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas sees first Mar '98 deals, nearbys slip.

text.p: The IPE natural gas futures market saw the March 1998 contract trade for the first time on Monday afternoon, with 60 lots traded in a range of prices between 14.10 pence and 14.35 pence a therm.
The last deal was done at 14.20 pence a therm, down by 0.47 pence from Friday's settlement price.

A futures broker pointed out that when a large volume of trade is done in the furthest forward month, it may mean that dealers are keen to transact trade in the period beyond that, for example the second quarter 1998.
This could lead to parties stacking up deals in the outermost month and then rolling forward their positions later.
In the near term, trade was thin, with only 30 lots traded all day in addition to the 60 done in March 1998.

April, June and September all saw small volumes of trade, with April and June slipping, as expected. April was traded at 9.90 pence a therm, breaking the psychologically important 10.00 pence barrier and maintaining the contango between the front months and the warmest months of the summer.
